subject: Build Pipeline Attestation & Secret Escrow Checklist
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex@assessco.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 19 Jun 2025 15:07:00 -0400
Subject: Request: build pipeline attestation & secrets escrow overview

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking this review. FinBank's external assessor (AssessCo) is compiling the SIG/SOC2 evidence pack and we need a focused attestation from Redwood on your build and deploy controls for the services you host for FinBank. Specifically, could you provide the following by next Thursday (26 Jun):

- CI/CD access matrix (who can push, who can approve, runner scopes). CSV or spreadsheet is fine.
- Evidence that deploys are gated (PR reviews, pre-deploy CI gates, and who has manual override). Screenshots or a short description + links acceptable.
- Secrets handling policy and how ephemeral credentials are used in runners. If you have a "secret escrow" or recovery process for long-lived keys, please include the policy doc.
- Audit traces for a sample deploy (one successful, one rollback) covering 30 May - 10 Jun. Logs or a zipped trace are fine (redact tokens).

If any of the above is sensitive, note the redaction and we'll coordinate secure transfer. Also let me know if you want AssessCo to accept a signed attestation rather than raw artifacts.

Appreciate a short response confirming scope and timeline.

Best,
Alex
AssessCo, Senior Assessor

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex@assessco.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 09:14:23 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: build pipeline attestation & secrets escrow overview

Alex — thanks for the clear list. We're on it and can deliver an evidence bundle by EOD Tue 24 Jun; if you absolutely need Thu 26 Jun we can push Friday for signatures.

Quick notes / constraints:
- The access matrix and runner roles export will be attached (ci-access-matrix-20250620.csv and runner-roles-snapshot-20250620.txt). Those are exports from our IAM and runner inventory.
- Our deploy gating combines PR reviews, required status checks, and an optional manual "safety" approval for production; I'll include the gate doc and a short annotated screenshot.
- "Secret escrow": we don't escrow production secrets centrally; we maintain long-lived customer-facing keys in HSM with rotation policies. We do maintain an encrypted backup policy and a documented emergency key recovery procedure — attaching secret-escrow-policy-v1.pdf.
- For audit traces, we will provide a sanitized pipeline-audit-trace-20250621.zip containing the CI build logs and deploy audit events (tokens redacted).

Jordan and Karthik — looping you both to confirm that the exported materials below are sufficient and to ask for the two sample deploy traces (one successful, one rollback) from the staging and prod pipelines. If anything is missing, flag it here.

Thanks,
Soojin
Director, Trust & Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ci-access-matrix-20250620.csv; runner-roles-snapshot-20250620.txt; secret-escrow-policy-v1.pdf

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 11:02:07 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: build pipeline attestation & secrets escrow overview

Soojin — got it. I pulled two traces this morning:
- staging deploy (success): pipeline id stg-20250531-443, included in pipeline-audit-trace-20250621.zip.
- prod deploy (rollback): pipeline id prod-20250603-77, included and redacted per policy.

Quick clarifications for AssessCo so they don't request raw tokens: the runner ephemeral creds are generated via short-lived service tokens (TTL=5m) issued from our internal token broker; long-lived keys are stored in HSM and require dual-approval rotation.

I'm also attaching a short snippet of the deploy gating rule that shows required status checks and reviewer count — it's in the CSV as a comment but I'll paste it here for convenience:

--- begin snippet ---
protection: required_checks=true; checks=[unit-tests,integration-tests,static-analysis]; reviewers_required=2; auto_merge=false
--- end snippet ---

Jordan
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachment: pipeline-audit-trace-20250621.zip

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Jun 2025 14:28:50 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: build pipeline attestation & secrets escrow overview

Adding a small operational note for the assessor:
- CI runners run in a segregated K8s cluster per environment (dev/staging/prod). Runner-role bindings are tied to an identity group; only members of the "platform-deployers" group have the ability to attach deploy credentials to a pipeline. Group membership changes require an approval ticket (JIRA:PLAT-334) and are audited.
- Secret rotation: automated rotation for service-to-service keys (90d) and manual rotation policy for HSM-backed customer keys (documented in the attached PDF).
- Recovery: emergency key recovery requires two platform leads + an audit log entry and is time-bounded; we keep an escrow copy encrypted with a customer-specific passphrase only accessible via KMS policy with MFA.

If AssessCo prefers a signed attestation instead of raw artifacts, I can draft the technical attestation (1 page) that enumerates controls and references the attached artifacts.

— Karthik
Staff Infra Engineer

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex@assessco.com>, Patricia Li <security@finbank.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Jun 2025 08:36:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: build pipeline attestation & secrets escrow overview

Alex / Patricia — attaching the compiled evidence bundle as promised. Contents summary:

1) ci-access-matrix-20250620.csv — IAM export of platform-deployers, reviewer groups, and approval rights.
2) runner-roles-snapshot-20250620.txt — runner scopes and platform node labeling.
3) pipeline-audit-trace-20250621.zip — sanitized traces: stg-20250531-443 (success) and prod-20250603-77 (rollback).
4) secret-escrow-policy-v1.pdf — policy describing HSM storage, recovery steps, and emergency escrow process.
5) one-page attestation (technical) drafted by Karthik (attached inline as text below) enumerating the controls and where to find corresponding artifacts.

Inline attestation (technical):
Redwood Inference affirms that the build and deploy controls in scope for FinBank-hosted services include: PR-based gating with required status checks (unit, integration, static analysis), reviewer minimum of 2, segregated CI runners per environment, ephemeral runner credentials (TTL=5m), HSM-backed storage for production keys with documented rotation and emergency recovery requiring dual-platform-lead approval and audit logging. Artifacts: ci-access-matrix-20250620.csv, runner-roles-snapshot-20250620.txt, pipeline-audit-trace-20250621.zip, secret-escrow-policy-v1.pdf.

If you'd like this on company letterhead with an authorized signature, tell me who at FinBank will accept that format and we'll route to Legal for signature.

Thanks — let me know if you need more granularity or a redaction workflow for particularly sensitive items.

Soojin
Director, Trust & Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ci-access-matrix-20250620.csv; runner-roles-snapshot-20250620.txt; secret-escrow-policy-v1.pdf; pipeline-audit-trace-20250621.zip
